title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: OPAL'S CAMERA
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Opal Whitfield, from Butte, Montana.
She runs the night laundry at the hospital.
Opal is so shy she says excuse me to the dryers.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SIGN-UP
segments.quote: A sheltered life can be a daring life as well. For all serious daring starts from within.
segments.author: Eudora Welty
lines: The library posted a sign: Faces of Butte, a photo show.
Opal wrote her name down, then reached for the eraser.
Her bookmark had a line from the writer Eudora Welty:
A sheltered life can be a daring life as well. For all serious daring starts from within.
She left her name, and bought a sixty-dollar pawnshop camera.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: TOO FAR AWAY
segments.quote: If your pictures aren't good enough, you're not close enough.
segments.author: Robert Capa
lines: Her first month: three hundred pictures of fences, from across the street.
Sid, the pawnshop owner, once shot for the newspaper. He quoted Robert Capa:
If your pictures aren't good enough, you're not close enough.
So Opal crossed the street and asked the pasty cart man. He said yes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: MR. NOVAK
segments.quote: Saturate yourself with your subject and the camera will all but take you by the hand.
segments.author: Margaret Bourke-White
lines: Then she met Mr. Novak, ninety, a retired miner who feeds pigeons downtown.
She snapped him once and ran. It looked like a scared tourist took it.
Sid tapped a card from Margaret Bourke-White:
Saturate yourself with your subject and the camera will all but take you by the hand.
So Opal sat with Mr. Novak every morning for a week, just listening.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: ONE GOOD ONE
segments.quote: Twelve significant photographs in any one year is a good crop.
segments.author: Ansel Adams
lines: Four hundred pictures. One was good. Mr. Novak laughing, a pigeon on his hat.
Opal felt like a failure. Sid pointed at a line from Ansel Adams:
Twelve significant photographs in any one year is a good crop.
One good one in a month? Sid said she was ahead of schedule.
She kept shooting.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE NIGHT CREW
segments.quote: I really believe there are things nobody would see if I didn't photograph them.
segments.author: Diane Arbus
lines: The library lady said, Maybe some mountains, hon? People love mountains.
But Opal thought of a line from the photographer Diane Arbus:
I really believe there are things nobody would see if I didn't photograph them.
So at three in the morning, she photographed her own crew. Folding. Laughing. Steam.
Nobody had ever taken their picture at work.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: OPENING NIGHT
segments.quote: The camera is an instrument that teaches people how to see without a camera.
segments.author: Dorothea Lange
lines: Opening night, the biggest crowd stood at her laundry photo, not the mountains.
Her crew cried. Mr. Novak brought a pigeon.
On the wall hung a line from Dorothea Lange:
The camera is an instrument that teaches people how to see without a camera.
Now Opal leads a free Saturday photo walk. Some days she leaves the camera home.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Dare from within. Get closer. Listen. Be patient. Show the unseen. Keep looking.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Dare from within. Get closer. Listen first. Be patient. Show the people nobody sees. Keep looking.
My wife says I photograph like a happy walrus. She's right.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
